analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump, the Nemotron Super inline-media body limit raised from 8 MiB to 40 MiB, and a new `media_too_large` code. The 40 MiB limit is described as holding one part at the shared 25 MiB inline-media cap as base64 plus every body the provider's transports deliver. Only head-side lines 533-544 and the context lines were visible; the head text of the video section (~lines 125-132) was not supplied, only the patch hunk.

Security consideration (TB-007, TB-003, T-050, T-028): a larger accepted encoded body raises potential memory pressure and DoS exposure. The documentation says the media reservation (decode, normalization, features, tower/projector bound) is taken from the shared budget before decoding, and that a charge the budget cannot hold gets a 503 before allocation. It also says only one image request runs at a time per owner (429 for a concurrent one). Together these suggest the larger limit does not bypass admission. I could not verify that the reservation is computed from the decoded dimensions before decoding, or that the encoded body is not buffered beyond the budget. The code (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes, the transport body caps, the MediaIngest/JPEG-PNG probe) was not supplied. Because this is a documentation-only change, I report no concrete regression.

Other content (prefix cache scoping by authenticated cache scope, no cache receipts for Super, the T-041 SSD tier, GLM5Next boundaries) is unchanged context. The documented statement that coordinator prefix reuse is partitioned by authenticated scope and off without one is consistent with T-041. No threat assumptions are invalidated by the supplied text.

Integration questions for deeper review: confirm that the code change matching this doc enforces the 40 MiB cap before base64 decode/buffer growth on both the coordinator WebSocket and local HTTP paths, and that the media reservation is applied before decoding.
